summary: Proxy ingress header rewrite + queued retry merge orphaned session pin during canary drain
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary drain in us-west-2, multiple tenant streaming sessions were observed to lose their pinned model affinity and begin routing to the legacy variant. Impact: Customer RelayDocs (enterprise) reported degraded outputs and a sudden usage/billing spike for affected sessions. Problem appears correlated with an edge ingress header rewrite that trims tenant routing hints when requests are merged from the ingress retry queue.

Environment: prod cluster in us-west-2, canary slice id=canary-2026-03-10-02, edge-proxy version v3.6.1, api-gateway v2.12.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Start long-lived streaming session pinned to redwood-open-7b-v1.
2) Trigger a canary drain (graceful prewarm drain) on a small subset of edge nodes.
3) Some requests hit an overloaded ingress node which defers and enqueues the request into the ingress retry/merge queue.
4) When ingress merges queued retries, the edge-proxy applies a header normalization (ingress-rewrite) that strips the last-of-key hint header: "x-tenant-route-hint" if it detects a long header chain.
5) Merged request reaches orchestrator without the tenant hint. Orchestrator cannot reconcile the existing session pin and falls back to routing heuristics, which send traffic to the legacy variant.

Expected behavior: Merge/retry logic should preserve session pin identity metadata (x-tenant-route-hint / x-session-pin) and merged requests should be routed to the pinned model variant.

Observed behavior: Clients experienced mixed outputs mid-stream (part of the stream from pinned model, subsequent frames from legacy variant). Telemetry shows the pin TTL remained active in the control plane but edge routing decided to route to fallback due to missing hint. Some sessions never re-established the pin resulting in continuous degraded routing until a new session was created.

Logs/evidence:
- Edge-proxy logs (edge-23) showing ingress-merge events at 2026-03-10T14:22:07Z with header_sanitizer:TRIM applied.
- Orchestrator trace for tenant relaydocs-17 showing route-decision: fallback_variant when x-tenant-route-hint=null.
- Serving runtime telemetry shows active pin lease for session s-8b9f but no incoming affinity token from edge for 7 minutes.
- Customer-provided recorded stream with timestamps mapping to variant switch at 2026-03-10T14:22:09Z.
comments: Support (Aisha): Initial report received from RelayDocs. Customer saw mixed generation outputs and unexpected cost increase during their heavy ingestion job. Raised to engineering and flagged as P1.

SRE (Luca): Reproduced on prod canary slice. Observed header trimming in ingress-merge path; will collect full edge-proxy logs and packet captures. Note: ingress-rewrite config recently hardened to remove duplicate headers (PR 2413).

Customer (RelayDocs): We observed 18 sessions impacted across multiple tenants, stream continuity broken. We have a post-hoc transcript if needed. Please prioritize — this affects production inference quality.

SRE (Luca): Temporary mitigation: disable ingress-merge header sanitization for canary slice via feature-flag ff/ingress-preserve-hint (rolled back at 2026-03-11T03:00Z). Early telemetry shows pinned routing resumed for new requests, but already-orphaned streams require reconnection.

Eng (Maya R.): Hypothesis: header sanitizer treats long header chains as suspicious and drops the last-of-key occurrence. Merged retry requests collapse headers and accidentally remove x-session-pin. Need codepath review in edge-proxy merge handler.
Support (Aisha): RelayDocs requested a timeline and whether they will be credited for the unexpected cost. Ticket owner to coordinate with billing.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC canary drain started. 14:22 ingress-merge queue flushed with header_sanitizer active. 14:22:09 first variant switch observed. Root cause likely regression in edge-proxy header merge logic introduced in PR 2413 (duplicate header removal) that did not preserve pinned-session header ordering. Evidence: packet capture shows x-session-pin present on initial request; absent on merged retry subset. Control plane retained pin leases — so this is purely edge-side metadata loss. Additional contributing factor: queue-merge uses last-of-key semantics when combining headers; session pinging uses the last header occurrence to indicate active pin (implementation detail).
Actions taken so far: disabled sanitizer flag for canary slice, collected edge logs, captured orchestrator decision traces, reproduced locally with simulated merge queue.
Next steps: patch edge-proxy merge logic to canonicalize headers without dropping last-of-key for x-session-pin / x-tenant-route-hint, add unit tests for merge behavior, and add a safety check in orchestrator to consult control-plane pin leases if hint missing for active stream.
resolution_notes:
Planned fix: revert aggressive duplicate-header prune for specific routing hint headers and add a defensive lookup in orchestrator to cross-check control-plane pin for active session ids. Patch branch: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/tree/fix/preserve-session-pin-merge. Target hotfix rollout to canary on 2026-03-13 and full rollout 2026-03-15 after verification.
Workarounds: 1) Customer reconnects streaming sessions to re-establish pins. 2) We temporarily disabled ff/ingress-preserve-hint on affected canary slice to preserve previous behavior.
Follow-ups: Billing review for unexpected token usage (assigned to Finance, ticket FIN-8842), add integration test for ingress-merge header preservation (assigned to QA), add monitoring alert when session pin TTL exists in control-plane but edge trace shows repeated route-decisions to fallback for same session (assigned to Observability).
notes: Avoid turning this ticket into a broad design doc; action items are implementation + tests + billing follow-up.
